product_brief: PQC enterprise VPN hosted on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure to safeguard data against classical and quantum threats.
pqc_capability_description: Combines PQC with advanced networking for CNSA 2.0, NIST Level 5 security. Uses MaxKyber® Protocol with exclusively CNSA 2.0 PQC algorithms. Provides post-quantum analog to Diffie-Hellman. Protects against Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later attacks.
key_management_model: Post-quantum analog to classical Diffie-Hellman methods; automated secure connection maintenance.
architecture_type: Enterprise VPN, virtual appliance (hosted on OCI), modular network protocol
primary_platforms: Mac, Windows, Android, iOS, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI)
regulatory_status: CNSA 2.0 aligned, NIST Level 5, CMMC compliance acceleration, SCCA Compliance
pqc_roadmap_details: Exclusively uses CNSA 2.0 PQC algorithms; aims to accelerate transition to quantum-safe infrastructure.
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: Compatible with bandwidth-limited use cases, such as mobile networks.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Low-friction; account setup and OCI endpoint installation in minutes; on-premises configurations within a day; single-click initiation.

product_brief: Network security platform building on WireGuard with automatic mesh configuration, SSO, NAT traversal, and centralized access control.
pqc_capability_description: Current implementation is not post-quantum secure and does not use PSKs. Tailscale cannot use ML-KEM directly in WireGuard due to lack of protocol agility. Future plan involves automatic PSK provisioning and distribution to devices to make Tailscale post-quantum secure out of the box.
crypto_primitives: WireGuard (asymmetric cryptography for handshake, symmetric key for connection encryption)
key_management_model: Automatic mesh configuration, single sign-on (SSO), centralized access control policies. Planned automatic PSK provisioning and distribution.
architecture_type: Builds on top of WireGuard; adds automatic mesh configuration, SSO, NAT traversal, TCP transport, and centralized access control policies.
pqc_roadmap_details: Intend to build automatic PSK provisioning and distribution to devices to allow Tailscale to be post-quantum secure out of the box in the future.

product_brief: Quantum-secure encryption integration for NVIDIA Jetson edge AI devices using the BLAST protocol and quantum-entropy key generation.
pqc_capability_description: The product uses the BLAST protocol, a peer-reviewed cryptographic protocol that generates identical encryption keys independently at each endpoint using quantum entropy, eliminating the need to transmit encryption keys across networks. It is described as "quantum-secure" and "quantum-ready on day one," addressing "harvest now, decrypt later" attacks. It utilizes a NIST-aligned cryptography stack and CNSA 2.0.
key_management_model: Independent key generation at each endpoint using quantum entropy; no key transmission across networks; automated key provisioning, rotation, and lifecycle management.
architecture_type: Software integration on hardware edge devices (NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano, Jetson Thor); custom Yocto Project kernel; end-to-end encryption from edge to data center.
fips_validated: Not stated (Note: Hardware QRNGs are NIST ESV certified; cryptography stack is CNSA 2.0 and NIST-aligned, but specific FIPS 140-2/3 validation status is not explicitly stated).
primary_platforms: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano, NVIDIA Jetson Thor, NVIDIA BlueField DPUs
target_industries: Robotics, autonomous systems, critical infrastructure, intelligence community, enterprise
pqc_roadmap_details: BLAST Protocol is available through Qrypt’s early access integration program.
qrng_&_entropy_sources: Hardware quantum random number generators; NIST ESV certified; quantum entropy sourced through exclusive licensing agreements with Oak Ridge and Los Alamos National Laboratories.
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: Designed for edge AI devices (Jetson Orin Nano, Jetson Thor); supports robotics and autonomous systems; built on custom Yocto Project kernel tailored to target devices.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Enables securing entire fleets of edge devices without rebuilding existing infrastructure; automates key provisioning and lifecycle management.

product_brief: VPN service offering quantum-resistant WireGuard connections using hybrid KEM algorithms for PresharedKey exchange.
pqc_capability_description: IVPN implements quantum-resistant WireGuard connections by using a hybrid Key Encapsulation Mechanism (KEM) to generate PresharedKeys. It uses multiple KEM algorithms: Kyber (Kyber-1024) and Classic McEliece (Classic-McEliece-348864). The PSK is calculated as the SHA256 sum of ciphers from both algorithms. This is integrated into the WireGuard key rotation phase via REST API over HTTPS.
crypto_primitives: AES, RSA, Diffie-Hellman, ECDH, ChaCha20, Poly1305, Curve25519, Kyber (Kyber-1024), Classic McEliece (Classic-McEliece-348864), SHA256
key_management_model: Hybrid KEM-based PresharedKey generation; PSK exchanged via REST API over HTTPS during WireGuard key regeneration; PSK calculated as SHA256 sum of multiple KEM ciphers.
architecture_type: Hybrid KEM (Kyber + Classic McEliece) for PSK generation in WireGuard
pqc_roadmap_details: IVPN currently uses Kyber-1024 and Classic-McEliece-348864 for hybrid KEM. The document states that in the future, it is expected that VPN protocols, including WireGuard, will incorporate post-quantum cryptography to provide enhanced security.
